story_log.title: Valkyries complete 16-point comeback to eliminate Wings 2-1 in WNBA first round — Gabby Williams takeover, Paige Bueckers season ends
story_log.development: CONTINUING [Day 3, TIER 1 ELIMINATION GAME]: Golden State rallied from 16 points down to beat Dallas 77-73 per ground truth, won series 2-1 per ground truth. Wings led 43-27 midway through 3rd quarter per ClutchPoints — Valkyries then went on 17-4 run per ClutchPoints, eventually 20-0 run per ClutchPoints. Williams: 19 PTS (17 in 2nd half, 11 in 4th quarter) per StatMuse/ClutchPoints — scored 2 PTS in 1st half, then took over. Arike Ogunbowale: 30 PTS, 5 REB, 11-21 FG per StatMuse — first player in Wings history with multiple 30-PT playoff games per StatMuse, 75 PTS over last two games (2nd-most in any two-game span in WNBA playoff history) per ClutchPoints. Bueckers: 17 PTS, 3-14 FG, 1-4 3PT per ClutchPoints — struggled in elimination game after 21 PTS on 9-10 FG in Game 1. Veronica Burton: 16 PTS, 10 REB, 6 AST per ClutchPoints. Tiffany Hayes: 18 PTS, 4 REB, 2 AST per ClutchPoints. Valkyries become first expansion team in league history to win playoff series in second season per StatMuse. Advance to face Aces in semifinals. Natalie Nakase went down while talking to officials, stayed on bench and led huddle per ClutchPoints/HaterReport — assistant Kasib Powell said she's fine, in great spirits per ClutchPoints. First-ever playoff series win in franchise history.

story_log.title: Pitt stuns Virginia Tech 35-33 after reliable Hokies kicker misses 36-yarder on final play — Pat Narduzzi rips AP voters
story_log.development: Pittsburgh beat Virginia Tech 35-33 per ground truth. VT kicker missed 36-yard FG on final play per CBS Sports. Controversial moment: ball appeared to sail directly over top of upright per RedditCFB/SharpFootball — not reviewable since it was above top of upright per NCAA Rule 12-3-1-b per RedditCFB. SharpFootball: 'how do we not have better ways to confirm FGs? this looks good to win the game, virtually everyone with good angle thinks it's good, but 1 dude staring up into cold night sky says it's not and we go with him without any review.' RedditCFB: 'Notably, there's nothing in NCAA rules preventing an arbitrarily tall upright. Virginia Tech may have won tonight if they'd made the uprights 100' tall.' Narduzzi ripped AP voters after win per CBS Sports. Panthers emerge as top threat to Miami in ACC per CBS Sports.

story_log.title: 0-4 Idaho stuns defending national champs Montana State after coach's timeout mistake — game ended at 2 AM ET in Moscow
story_log.development: Idaho beat Montana State per ground truth (score not provided, but RedditCFB confirms upset). Idaho 0-4, Montana State 5-0 defending national champs entering game per RedditCFB. Idaho caught pass in-bounds for first down at 25 with 0:01 left, down 7 per RedditCFB — no time to spike ball. Montana State coach Brent Vigen called timeout, giving Idaho one more play per RedditCFB. Idaho caught TD, went for 2, converted per RedditCFB. Game ended at 2 AM ET in Moscow, Idaho per RedditCFB. SharpFootball: 'one of the WORST coaching decisions you will ever see — the Montana State coach LOST HIS TEAM THE GAME — worst timeout EVER.' RedditCFB: 'IDAHO HAS DONE IT ARE YOU KIDDING ME!!!! 0-4 IDAHO UPSETS 5-0 DEFENDING NATIONAL CHAMPS MONTANA STATE!!! AND THEY SHOULDN'T EVEN HAVE HAD THE CHANCE BUT MONTANA STATE GAVE IT TO THEM!!!' Game literally in Moscow per RedditCFB.

story_log.title: 49ers owner Jed York suspended 6 games, fined $500K for violating NFL Personal Conduct Policy — stemming from August prostitution arrest
story_log.development: NFL suspended York for six regular-season games and fined him $500K per AdamSchefter/TomPelissero/ESPN/AlbertBreer. Stemming from August arrest on suspicion of engaging in prostitution in Ohio per ESPN. York stayed away from 49ers' first three regular-season games and NFL league meetings during investigation per AdamSchefter — those three games count toward suspension, may return Oct 20 per AdamSchefter. York statement: 'Today, the NFL concluded its review, and I accept its decision in full. To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry. This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one's failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don't take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead.' per AdamSchefter.

story_log.title: College basketball eligibility battles continue — Kentucky court dissolves injunction, NCAA appeals West Virginia ruling, Missouri's Mark Mitchell among players affected
story_log.development: CONTINUING: Kentucky Court of Appeals dissolved temporary injunction that had been basis for eligibility per JonRothstein/CBS Sports — leaves Mark Mitchell (Missouri), Seth Trimble (Louisville), Fred King (Creighton), Skyy Clark (LSU) and others ineligible per JonRothstein. NCAA will appeal preliminary injunction that allowed West Virginia's Brenen Lorient and Javan Buchanan to be immediately eligible per JonRothstein. LSU's Clark will now attempt to seek eligibility through California case per JonRothstein — preliminary injunction hearing in California continues Oct 20 per JonRothstein. NCAA released statement per JonRothstein. JonRothstein: 'One thing we've learned in last 60 days? The NCAA is not just going to roll over and allow the Class of 2022 to play in 2026-27. Everything will continue to be challenged legally in court.' Season starts in 29 days per JonRothstein.

lead_story.headline: Golden State rallies from 16 down to shock Dallas, advance to semifinals

lead_story.research_notes: CONTINUING [Day 3]: Reader knows the series was tied 1-1 after Arike's historic 45-point Game 2. New today: Golden State's miraculous 16-point comeback in elimination game, Gabby Williams' second-half takeover (2 in 1H, 17 in 2H), Paige Bueckers' season-ending shooting slump (3-14 FG in Game 3 after 9-10 in Game 1), and the Valkyries becoming the first expansion team in WNBA history to win a playoff series in their second season. TIER 1 ELIMINATION GAME: this is a must-lead story per the calendar rules — a first-round Game 3 where one team could be eliminated. The comeback itself is the hook: Dallas led 43-27 midway through the third, then Valkyries went on a 20-0 run. Williams scored 11 of her 17 second-half points in the 4th quarter to seal it. Arike had another monster game (30 PTS, 75 over last two games = 2nd-most in any two-game span in playoff history) but it wasn't enough. Bueckers' playoff struggles: after a perfect 9-10 FG in Game 1, she went 3-13 in Game 2 and 3-14 in Game 3 — that's the storyline for Dallas fans. The Valkyries' historic milestone: first expansion team to win a series in Year 2. Natalie Nakase went down talking to officials, stayed on bench — assistant said she's fine. Cross-sport parallels: expansion teams breaking through (Vegas Golden Knights 2018 Stanley Cup Final, Jacksonville Jaguars 2017 AFC title game). Meme angle: the 'switch flipped' per CBS Sports headline. GIF seed: the Valkyries' belief in each other per Gabby Williams quote. Player reputation: Paige as the face of the league coming up short in the biggest moment. Financial absurdity: the Valkyries are a second-year expansion franchise and just eliminated a team with the WNBA's leading scorer. The Aces await in the semifinals — A'ja Wilson vs. the upstart Valkyries is the next chapter.

supporting_stories.research_notes: The hook: defending national champion Brent Vigen called a timeout that GAVE Idaho one more play with 0:01 left, down 7 — Idaho caught a TD and converted the 2-point conversion to win. SharpFootball: 'one of the WORST coaching decisions you will ever see — the Montana State coach LOST HIS TEAM THE GAME — worst timeout EVER.' The absurdity: Idaho was 0-4, Montana State was 5-0 and the defending FCS champs. The game ended at 2 AM ET in Moscow, Idaho. RedditCFB: 'IDAHO HAS DONE IT ARE YOU KIDDING ME!!!! 0-4 IDAHO UPSETS 5-0 DEFENDING NATIONAL CHAMPS MONTANA STATE!!! AND THEY SHOULDN'T EVEN HAVE HAD THE CHANCE BUT MONTANA STATE GAVE IT TO THEM!!!' The timeout mistake: Idaho caught a pass in-bounds for a first down at the 25 with 0:01 left — no time to spike the ball, game should have ended. Vigen called timeout, giving Idaho one more play. Meme angle: the Chris Webber timeout comparison per RedditCFB. Cross-sport parallel: the worst timeout calls in sports history (Chris Webber 1993, Ice Bowl). The financial stakes: this could cost Montana State a playoff seed. The late-night absurdity: everyone watching this at 2 AM ET in a dome in Moscow, Idaho.
